svg.aria-label: How to write б, д: 2 letters, б, д, one after another
svg.title: Writing б, д
svg.desc: 2 letters written one after another: б, д (cyrillic). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansCyrillic-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: б: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase б demonstration, 01:13–01:18, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>; д: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase д demonstration, 02:14–02:19, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>. Source notes on variation: б: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 01:13–01:18 lowercase б demonstration, the pen circles the lower body counterclockwise, closes it at the upper-right junction, and continues through the rising shoulder into the rightward top flag in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand crosses diagonally from the body's upper-right junction toward the rising shoulder; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph joins its ascender through the body's upper-left shoulder instead. This learner path preserves the source's uninterrupted body-to-flag order while routing that transition along the printed upper shoulder so it remains on the font's ink. Connected cursive may lengthen the top flag into an exit join, and individual handwriting may narrow, round, or slant the lower body differently. д: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 02:14–02:19 lowercase д demonstration, the pen circles the rounded body counterclockwise, closes it at the upper-right junction, descends below the baseline, loops left, and rises into the rightward exit in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand resembles a looped Latin cursive g; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a block-like printed form with a trapezoidal body, a joined base shelf, and two separated feet rather than one descender loop. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-descender order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed form: circle the body, descend through the right stem and foot, retrace to the shelf, sweep left, retrace the left foot, and finish rightward along the shelf without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's below-baseline loop and exit join, and individual handwriting may narrow, round, or slant the body and loop differently.
svg.text: How it is written — 2 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Letter 2 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase б demonstration,
Letter 2: stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase д demonstration,
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
